claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and any children you're supporting.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under your care that you'd like me to check eligibility for?** If so, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'd like to check about my son Alex. He's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know about Alex, who is 6 years old.

To help me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather a bit more information about your circumstances.

**Are you currently living in the UK, and do you have a UK National Insurance number?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK at the moment. I'm living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful information.

**Could you tell me which country you're currently living in?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm currently living in Spain.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know you're in Spain.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I am a British citizen, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. Thank you.

**Is Alex's other parent (or the other parent of any children you're claiming for) a British citizen or do they have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about their exact status at the moment, but Alex doesn't live with me - he lives with his other parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that important clarification. That's a key detail.

**Can you confirm whether you are providing financial support for Alex, or are you looking to claim Child Benefit for another reason?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do provide financial support for Alex. I send money regularly to help with his upkeep - things like clothes, school supplies, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's useful information.

**Does Alex live in the UK with his other parent, or does he live elsewhere (such as in Spain or another country)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives in the UK with his other parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's very helpful to know. Thank you.

**Are you currently working or paying National Insurance contributions, either in Spain or through any UK employment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm working here in Spain at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Are you paying National Insurance contributions through your UK National Insurance number while working in Spain, or are you only paying contributions to Spain?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm only paying contributions here in Spain.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

**One more question to help me complete my assessment: Are you the person with primary responsibility for Alex's day-to-day care and upbringing, or is his other parent the primary caregiver?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: His other parent is the primary caregiver - Alex lives with them full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all of that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review your circumstances against the Child Benefit eligibility rules:

- You are a British citizen living in Spain
- You are working in Spain and paying Spanish National Insurance contributions only
- Alex is 6 years old and lives in the UK with his other parent
- You provide financial support to Alex, but you are not his primary caregiver
- Alex's other parent has primary responsibility for his day-to-day care

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility criteria, I'm now ready to provide my outcome.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

The main reason is that Child Benefit is payable to the person who has primary responsibility for the day-to-day care and upbringing of the child. Since Alex lives full-time with his other parent in the UK, and they are his primary caregiver, they would be the appropriate person to claim Child Benefit for him.

While it's commendable that you provide financial support to Alex, providing maintenance payments alone doesn't qualify you for Child Benefit. Additionally, your residence in Spain and the fact that you're only paying National Insurance contributions there (rather than in the UK) also affects your eligibility.

**I would recommend that Alex's other parent—the one with whom he lives in the UK—explores whether they are eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.** If you have any questions about this outcome or need further guidance, feel free to ask.
